verses.verse:
कायशौचम् मनः शुद्धिः प्राणः सोधम् समाचरेत्।
जिज्ञासुर्गुरुमाश्रित्य संगीतज्ञः सुखी भवेत्।१३२।
verses.text: One should practise cleanliness of body, purity of mind and purification of the breath; the seeker who takes refuge in a guru becomes a happy musician.

commentary.text: Having gained cleanliness and health of the body, having washed with the soap of faith the mind soiled by impurities such as attachment and aversion, and then having freed the prāṇa (life-breath) and the mind and intellect from restlessness through prāṇāyāma (breath control) and the like - when the desire to know arises in the mind, only then does one search for a guru (teacher). And only by gaining knowledge from the guru does the musician find happiness and peace. So keep the temple of your mind always lit with the lamp of goodwill and faith; otherwise, like insects and vermin in an empty house, many enemies such as hatred, pride, envy and anger will enter that temple of the mind uninvited. Then, instead of good (artha), only harm (anartha) can come. Then, in that corrupted mind, even separate knowledge of word, rāga and tāla will become impossible. Then the confluence of these three will be as far from them as the confluence at Prayāg is for base people living at that place of pilgrimage: though within reach, it remains out of reach. The subject from here on is somewhat deep, so keep your mind safe from faults and make it pure, so that one may enjoy it properly. In the next śloka the difference between gat and gīt is described.
